visuals.heading: Social Science Degree Actually Opens Up

items.text: Social science leads to at least 7 real tracks across sociology, economics, social work, and anthropology, not two.
The list below is ordered by real growth and growth headroom, based on how each track actually pays as you gain seniority and proof, not by which one sounds most respectable at a family gathering.
Independent advisory to CSR teams, foundations, multilateral bodies and government departments on programme design, monitoring, and impact evaluation.
Economics graduates move into equity research, credit risk, RBI/SEBI-adjacent policy work, and corporate strategy teams.
This is the track most sociology, social work, and public-policy students never hear about, and it is the one with the most genuine room to scale.

A smaller but related version of the same idea: building an independent research or commentary platform, a data-driven policy newsletter, a social-research consulting practice, or an evaluation specialism you own outright rather than deliver under someone else's brand.

Why this scales when the others don't: you set your own pricing instead of sitting on a fixed NGO or government pay band, demand repeats every funding or reporting cycle rather than depending on one employer's budget, and once you have a track record you can bring on junior researchers instead of doing every hour of work yourself.
Two tracks on this list share a pattern the "just clear the exam" framing hides completely: clearing the first, well-known filter does not end the competition.
You need to clear UGC-NET/JRF in your subject, then get into a PhD programme with real funding.
Finishing the PhD does not guarantee a permanent seat.
Before you commit real years, a NET-JRF attempt, a PhD, an unpaid internship season, a CDPO exam, run the track you are leaning toward through The four questions .
MSW fieldwork means home visits, hospital wards, correctional facilities, and sitting with people in crisis.
UGC-NET/PhD prep, unpaid NGO internships, and RBI Grade B or CDPO exam preparation all assume months to years of low or no income while you build the credential.

blocks.heading: Building Proof Before You Commit Years

items.text: A qualification checklist tells you what is formally required.
Do not start NET-JRF prep, enrol in a PhD, or take a CDPO-exam coaching package before passing all three proofs below.

One published research note, one programme-evaluation write-up, or one anonymised case study written to a real organisation's format, not a general statement that you "care about people" or "like data."
Corporate government-affairs-style CSR leadership, BFSI research, and independent policy consulting quietly outpay both of them once you build real proof.
A generic MSW or MA in Sociology gives you a foundation, not a job.
A funded seat, a realistic timeline, and an honest look at how many recent graduates from your target department actually got permanent posts matter more than the prestige of the university name.

Equity and credit research, macro and policy research, consulting, think tanks, PhD and teaching.
Econometrics with code, a sector specialisation, and writing that a non-economist can follow.

blocks.heading: Realistic Pay Across All 7 Tracks
rows: Policy & social-impact consulting (independent)
Highly variable, upside-driven

Income scales with your client base and project pipeline, not a salary band. Junior researcher roles at established consultancies pay a fixed project or retainer fee; senior, client-facing consultants set their own pricing.
Economics: research, policy & BFSI
Entry ~₹4-8L (research analyst); manager/senior BFSI roles considerably higher

RBI Grade B carried around 120 officer vacancies in the 2025 cycle across the General, DEPR (economics), and DSIM (statistics) streams, on a fixed central Group B pay scale from roughly ₹55,000-60,000/month basic. Private BFSI research and strategy roles pay a wide range above this once you clear the entry filter.
CSR leadership & ESG
Entry analyst ~₹6-10L; manager/lead level ~₹18-30L+

Current job-board listings for CSR Manager and ESG Manager roles at large Indian companies typically show this spread, depending heavily on company size, sector, and whether the role sits inside a listed company with formal ESG reporting obligations.
Social work (MSW): NGO & welfare roles
Entry modest, roughly ₹2.5-4.5L; rises slowly without specialisation

Programme-officer-level pay at most Indian NGOs is modest and tied to project funding cycles. Medical and psychiatric social work in larger hospitals, and CSR-execution roles for corporates, pay meaningfully more once you specialise.
Sociology: research agencies & UX research
Entry ~₹4-8L; rises with method and data-analysis depth

Corporate market-research and UX-research roles pay considerably better than classic academic or NGO sociology research at the same experience level, because the same interview and observation skill is now billed to product and brand teams.
Anthropology: ASI/ANSI & ethnographic research
Government scale for confirmed posts; UX/ethnographic research pay similar to Track 5

Archaeological Survey of India and Anthropological Survey of India posts follow the applicable central pay-matrix level for the specific grade. Ethnographic UX-research work in the private sector generally follows sociology-adjacent research pay above.

blocks.heading: AI Is Doing to Social Science Careers

items.text: Routine survey coding and open-ended response tagging, sorting hundreds of free-text answers into themes, is already shifting into AI-assisted workflows at research agencies and CSR teams.
First-pass literature review summaries and basic transcription of interviews or focus groups are easier to automate than the interpretation that follows them.
Basic economic data cleaning and first-draft chart generation, turning a raw government dataset into a readable table, is now largely a tool problem AI handles faster than a fresher can by hand.

blocks.heading: Skills That Matter on Every Track

items.text: Research method and data literacy , comfort with survey design, interview technique, and basic statistical or spreadsheet analysis.
Clear, plain-language writing , a policy brief, an impact report, or a case note is worthless if only other specialists can follow it. This is the proof format most of these tracks actually hire on.
Field and relationship judgment , the human layer behind social work, CSR execution, and consulting that AI does not touch.

Programme and monitoring-and-evaluation thinking , the ability to define what "worked" actually means and measure it, which is exactly what turns fieldwork experience into CSR or consulting-level pay.
Practical AI fluency , using AI tools to speed up coding, transcription, and drafting while personally verifying every output, per the AI section above.
